studies.title: Effects of Urolithin A supplementation on muscle health outcomes in humans from randomized controlled trials.
studies.abstract: Urolithin A (UA), a gut microbiota-derived metabolite, has been proposed to improve skeletal muscle function, but evidence from randomized controlled trials has not been systematically summarized. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of UA supplementation on muscle performance as well as biochemical and mitochondrial biomarkers in humans. Randomized controlled trials published up to December 2025 were identified through systematic searches of four electronic databases: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus. Trials comparing oral UA supplementation with placebo and reporting muscle-related outcomes were included. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, and the certainty of evidence for the primary quantitatively synthesized outcome was rated using the GRADE approach. Quantitative meta-analysis was feasible only for the 6-min walk test (6MWT); remaining outcomes were synthesized narratively. For multi-arm trials with a shared comparator, intervention arms were combined into a single group following Cochrane Handbook guidance to avoid unit-of-analysis errors. Pooled mean differences with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using inverse-variance weighting, with both fixed-effect and random-effects sensitivity analyses. Five randomized controlled trials ( The currently available randomized human evidence is limited to five small, short-term trials in clinically heterogeneous populations. Quantitative pooling was feasible for a single outcome (6MWT) based on two trials and showed a directionally favorable but statistically inconclusive effect with low GRADE certainty. Narrative findings on strength, endurance, and mitochondrial-related biomarkers are exploratory and hypothesis-generating, not reproducible evidence of efficacy. Larger, longer, and methodologically standardized trials in better-defined populations are required before firm clinical recommendations can be made. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251270987, identifier: PROSPERO 2025 CRD420251270987.

studies.title: Evaluating the Impact of Urolithin A Supplementation on Running Performance, Recovery, and Mitochondrial Biomarkers in Highly Trained Male Distance Runners.
studies.abstract: Urolithin A (UA) is a metabolite produced by gut bacteria following the consumption of ellagitannin-rich foods. Clinical trials in middle-aged and older adults demonstrated that supplementation with UA improves muscle strength, endurance, and biomarkers of mitochondrial health, suggesting that UA may be an effective ergogenic aid in other populations. In this double-blind, parallel group, placebo-controlled clinical trial (NCT04783207), competitive male distance runners (n = 42, 27.2 ± 1.0 years,  Running performance (3000 m time trial) was not significantly improved in either treatment group (UA; p = 0.116, PL; p = 0.771), although UA supplementation significantly lowered ratings of perceived exertion (RPE, p = 0.02) and reduced indirect markers of post-exercise muscle damage (CK, total area under the curve p < 0.0001) following the 3000 m time trial compared with PL. Although there was no statistically significant time × treatment interaction for aerobic capacity (p = 0.138), UA supplementation showed a large within-group increase in  Our results show that 4 weeks of daily UA supplementation facilitates recovery by downregulating inflammatory pathways and indirect markers of muscle damage. However, despite a reduction in rating of exertion and increased aerobic capacity, UA supplementation did not further enhance performance in highly trained male endurance athletes.

studies.title: Urolithin A improves muscle function by inducing mitophagy in muscular dystrophy.
studies.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is the most common muscular dystrophy, and despite advances in genetic and pharmacological disease-modifying treatments, its management remains a major challenge. Mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to DMD, yet the mechanisms by which this occurs remain elusive. Our data in experimental models and patients with DMD show that reduced expression of genes involved in mitochondrial autophagy, or mitophagy, contributes to mitochondrial dysfunction. Mitophagy markers were reduced in skeletal muscle and in muscle stem cells (MuSCs) of a mouse model of DMD. Administration of the mitophagy activator urolithin A (UA) rescued mitophagy in DMD worms and mice and in primary myoblasts from patients with DMD, increased skeletal muscle respiratory capacity, and improved MuSCs' regenerative ability, resulting in the recovery of muscle function and increased survival in DMD mouse models. These data indicate that restoration of mitophagy alleviates symptoms of DMD and suggest that UA may have potential therapeutic applications for muscular dystrophies.

studies.title: Effect of urolithin A on the improvement of vascular endothelial function depends on the gut microbiota.
studies.abstract:
Background

Urolithin A (UA) is a metabolite produced by gut microbiota from ingested ellagic acid. Although the effect of ellagic acid intake on vascular endothelial function (VEF) improvement has been reported, the effect of UA intake on VEF improvement remains obscure. In addition, UA has been reported to improve the intestinal barrier function, and UA may have improved VEF by gut microbiome alteration.

Objective

In this study, we conducted a clinical trial to explore and analyze the effects of UA intake on vascular endothelial function (VEF) and characteristics of the intestinal environment, such as gut microbiome profiling and organic acid composition.

Methods

A placebo-controlled, randomized, double-blinded, parallel group trial was conducted on participants who could metabolize small amounts of UA from ellagic acid (non-UA producers) and had relatively poor VEF. VEF was assessed using the flow-mediated vasodilatation (FMD) score. Participants were administered placebo, UA 10 mg/day, or UA 50 mg/day for 12 weeks. FMD was measured and fecal samples were collected at 0, 4, 8, and 12 weeks of treatment. Gut microbiome analysis and organic acid level measurements were performed to evaluate the effects of UA intake on the intestinal environment. This clinical trial is publicly registered at the UMIN-CTR, trial number: UMIN000042014.

Results

The gut microbiota of the UA 50 mg/day group showed a significant increase in alpha diversity (Faith's phylogenetic diversity). Four and nine microbial genera were significantly altered in the UA 10 mg/day and UA 50 mg/day groups, respectively (p < 0.05, not corrected). Participants whose FMD scores improved with UA intake had poor baseline FMD values as well as a low Bacillota/Bacteroidota ratio.

Conclusion

Urolithin A intake alters the gut microbiota and improves their alpha diversity. In addition, the effect of UA on VEF correlated with the individual gut microbiota. Our results have practical implications for a new approach to providing healthcare that focuses on intestinal environment-based diet therapy.

studies.title: Targeting PKGIα Cys<sup>42</sup> attenuates cardiac dysfunction in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
studies.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a highly prevalent condition associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, yet effective therapeutic options remain limited. As oxidation of Cys<sup>42</sup> in cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP)-dependent protein kinase Iα (PKGIα) can enhance vessel and diastolic relaxation, processes impaired in HFpEF, we sought to target this mechanism using natural compounds with predicted thiol reactivity. Among these, urolithin A emerged as a compound with a previously unidentified and counterintuitive mode of action, directly modifying Cys<sup>42</sup> in PKGIα. In a multihit HFpEF model that closely mimics the human condition, urolithin A improved diastolic function and attenuated cardiac remodeling through cysteine 42-dependent activation of PKGIα. These findings were further validated in human engineered heart tissue, where urolithin A enhanced both relaxation and contraction kinetics. These findings collectively highlight Cys<sup>42</sup> in PKGIα as a promising therapeutic target for HFpEF and identify urolithin A as a previously unidentified activator of this protective mechanism.

studies.title: Antidiabetic Effect of Urolithin A in Cultured L6 Myotubes and Type 2 Diabetic Model KK-A<sup>y</sup>/Ta Mice with Glucose Intolerance.
studies.abstract: Diabetes is caused by abnormal glucose metabolism, and muscle, the largest tissue in the human body, is largely involved. Urolithin A (UroA) is a major intestinal and microbial metabolite of ellagic acid and ellagitannins and is found in fruits such as strawberry and pomegranate. In this present study, we investigated the antidiabetic effects of UroA in L6 myotubes and in KK-A<sup>y</sup>/Ta, a mouse model of type 2 diabetes (T2D). UroA treatment elevated the glucose uptake (GU) of L6 myotubes in the absence of insulin. This elevation in GU by UroA treatment was partially inhibited by the concurrent addition of LY294002, an inhibitor of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) which activates Akt (PKB: protein kinase B) or Compound C, an inhibitor of 5'-adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK). Moreover, UroA was found to activate both pathways of Akt and AMPK, and then to promote translocation of glucose transporter 4 (GLUT4) from the cytosol to the plasma membrane in L6 myotubes. Based on these in vitro findings, an intraperitoneal glucose tolerance test (IPGTT) was performed after the oral administration of UroA for 3 weeks to KK-A<sup>y</sup>/Ta mice with glucose intolerance. UroA was demonstrated to alleviate glucose intolerance. These results suggest that UroA is a biofactor with antihyperglycemic effects in the T2D state.

studies.title: Urolithin A supplementation improves chronic sleep deprivation-induced cognitive impairments and anxiety in mice by suppressing hippocampal ferroptosis via the
studies.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) is now a widespread issue affecting people globally. It adversely impacts individuals of all ages, contributing to cognitive deficits and increased anxiety. Urolithin A (UA) has been found to address numerous health concerns, including the preservation of brain function. Nonetheless, the exact mechanisms by which UA counters cognitive deficits and anxiety resulting from SD are not well understood. To investigate the specific molecular mechanisms involving the Nrf2-ferroptosis axis through which UA ameliorates cognitive impairments and anxiety-like behaviors resulting from prolonged SD. A murine model of chronic SD was generated by implementing sleep restriction for a duration of 14 consecutive days (n=15 per group). Behavioral experiments were used to assess the success of the SD model and the therapeutic impact of UA. We explored the mechanisms using spatial metabolites and biological functional module network analysis. Furthermore, erastin was utilized to induce ferroptosis in HT-22 cells, creating a model to assess the ferroptosis inhibition effects of UA. UA treatment (100 mg/kg, i.g.) significantly mitigated behavioral abnormalities caused by chronic SD. UA prevented both histopathological alterations and structural injury to hippocampal neurons (P < 0.05, P < 0.01). Further analyses revealed that UA not only attenuated excessive neuroinflammation but also increased dendritic spine density and the protein levels of neurotrophic factors in the hippocampus of chronic SD mice. Mechanistically, spatial metabolomics and target prediction analyses further revealed that the effects of UA were closely associated with the Nrf2 signaling pathway and ferroptosis suppression. UA treatment significantly decreased total iron and Fe Overall, supplementation with UA proved beneficial in counteracting chronic SD-induced cognitive deterioration and anxiety-like behaviors by attenuating hippocampal ferroptosis through the Nrf2 pathway. These results suggested that UA represents a potential candidate for future translational studies addressing cognitive impairments and anxiety related to insufficient sleep.

studies.title: Ameliorative Effects of Urolithin A Against Cadmium-Induced NLRP3-Mediated Pyroptosis and Cognitive Deficits Via Regulating Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor Signaling.
studies.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is an important environmental and industrial pollutant that induces neurotoxicity and neurobehavioral disorders in animals. Urolithin A (UA), a gut microbial-derived metabolite from polyphenolic compounds, exhibits potent neuroprotective effects in neurological disorders. Herein, we evaluated the ameliorative impact of UA on Cd exposure-evoked hippocampal injury and cognitive deficits in mice and disclosed the underlying molecular mechanisms. C57BL/6J mice were randomly divided into four groups: Control, CdCl₂, CdCl₂ + UA, and UA. CdCl₂ (1 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally for 8 weeks. UA (200 mg/kg) was given by gavage 2 h prior to CdCl₂ treatment. SH-SY5Y cells were pretreated with UA followed by 20 μM CdCl₂ exposure. Behavioral tests (Morris water maze, Y-maze, Novel object recognition), Nissl staining, Immunofluorescence, Western blot, transmission electron microscopy, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) detection, and Flow cytometry were used to assess cognitive function, neuronal/synaptic damage, and molecular signaling. The results demonstrated that UA administration markedly mitigated hippocampal neuronal/synaptic injury and cognitive impairments in Cd-exposed mice. Mechanically, UA administration suppressed Cd exposure-triggered activation of the NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome and subsequent neuronal pyroptosis in mice hippocampi and SH-SY5Y cells. Moreover, UA administration inhibited Cd-induced AhR activation and reduced the expression of CYP1A1, leading to mtROS elimination in vivo and in vitro. In conclusion, our findings revealed that UA mitigated Cd stress-driven aberrant NLRP3 inflammasome activation and its-mediated neuronal pyroptosis by promoting mtROS clearance, partly via the inhibition of the AhR-CYP1A1 signaling pathway, which ultimately contributed to the attenuation of neuronal/synaptic damage and cognitive deficits.

studies.title: Neuroprotective effects of Urolithin A and B in an intracerebroventricular streptozotocin-induced Alzheimer's-like model in rats.
studies.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD), a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by amyloid beta and tau protein aggregation, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation. Urolithin A (Uro A) and Urolithin B (Uro B), known for their anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and neuroprotective properties, are promising therapeutic candidates for AD. This study evaluated the effects of Uro A and Uro B on memory, anxiety-like behaviors, brain oxidative stress markers, and histopathological changes in male rats subjected to streptozotocin (STZ)-induced AD. Wistar rats were divided into eight groups (n = 7) and treated with Uro A or Uro B (10 or 20 mg/kg), memantine (positive control), or vehicle control for 14 days following intracerebroventricular STZ injection. Behavioral tests, biochemical analyses, and histological evaluations were conducted after six weeks. Modest improvements in memory performance were observed (p < 0.05) in the shuttle box test and reduced anxiety-like behaviors in the elevated plus-maze test. Biochemical analyses revealed decreased oxidative stress markers (malondialdehyde and hydroperoxides) and increased total antioxidant capacity (p < 0.05). Also, it seems that both compounds can reduce necrotic neurons and amyloid-like depositions in the hippocampus and cerebral cortex, and no adverse effects on the histology of the liver, kidney, pancreas, and testis were observed. These findings demonstrate the therapeutic potential of Uro A and Uro B in ameliorating cognitive deficits, oxidative stress, and neuronal damage in AD. Further studies are needed to explore the mechanisms underlying these effects and their applicability in clinical contexts.

studies.title: Neuroprotective effect of Urolithin A via downregulating VDAC1-mediated autophagy in Alzheimer's disease.
studies.abstract: Amyloid β (Aβ) accumulation in the brains of patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) contributes to cognitive impairment and neuronal damage. Urolithin A (UA), a gut microbiota-derived metabolite of ellagic acid, has been reported to cross the blood-brain barrier to exert anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidation effects in the brain. However, the molecular mechanisms of UA in AD were still unclear. This study aims to explore the neuroprotective effect and mechanism of UA on APP/PS1 mice and Aβ In this study, Morris water maze was used to detect the cognitive function. Immunofluorescence was used to detect the deposition of Aβ and the expression of voltage-dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1) in the brains of APP/PS1 mice. Western blotting was used to detect the expression of VDAC1, AMPK pathway, PI3K pathway and autophagy-related proteins. CCK8 was used to detect the viability of Aβ In this research, we found that UA improved cognitive dysfunction and reduced Aβ deposition in APP/PS1 mice. Furthermore, UA activated autophagy and upregulated the levels of autophagy-related proteins in both APP/PS1 mice and Aβ These findings demonstrated that UA down-regulated VDAC1 played a key neuroprotective role on AD by inhibiting the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and activating the AMPK pathway to promote autophagy.

studies.title: Urolithin A improves Parkinson's disease-associated cognitive impairment through modulation of neuroinflammation and neuroplasticity.
studies.abstract: Cognitive impairment is one of the most common disabling non-motor manifestations of Parkinson's disease (PD), an age-onset condition for which there are no effective therapies available to date. Urolithin A (UA) is a natural compound produced by gut bacteria from ingested ellagitannins (ETs) and ellagic acid (EA). Our previous study showed that UA ameliorates motor deficits and dopaminergic neurodegeneration in experimental models of PD. However, its effect on PD non-motor symptoms has not been elucidated. This study aims to explore the effect of UA on cognitive impairment in MPTP-induced PD mouse model as well as in transgenic mice that overexpresses human A53T mutant α-synuclein (A53T mice). Treatment with UA reversed cognitive dysfunction as measured by Morris water maze, Y maze and novel object recognition tests in both PD models. Enhanced cognition was associated with decreased neuroinflammation in the hippocampus. Additionally, UA also reduced hippocampal neuronal dendritic spine loss and synaptic damage. Further mechanistic analyses revealed that the beneficial effects of UA on cognitive impairment appears to involve the activation of the highly protective AKT/CREB/BDNF signaling pathway. Collectively, these findings strongly suggest that UA mitigates cognitive deficits in both MPTP-induced PD mouse model and A53T mice by reducing neuroinflammation and sustaining neuroplasticity. This study provides the first evidence for a potential therapeutic effect of UA on cognitive impairment in vivo, and supports further assessment for the possible use of UA as a dietary supplement to prevent cognitive deficits in PD, and related neurodegenerative diseases.

studies.title: Urolithin A alleviates schizophrenic-like behaviors and cognitive impairment in rats through modulation of neuroinflammation, neurogenesis, and synaptic plastic
studies.abstract: Cognitive impairment in schizophrenia occurs in the early stages of the disease and is closely associated with prognosis. Alleviation of cognitive impairment in schizophrenia faces major challenges owing to the lack of preventive and therapeutic drugs that are novel and effective. Urolithin A (UA) is a gut microbial metabolite of ellagic acid that has demonstrated neuroprotective effects in multiple neurological disease models. Nonetheless, the neuromodulatory role of UA in schizophrenia is yet to be elucidated. Wistar rat pups were separated from their mothers for 24 h on postnatal days (PNDs) 9-10 to establish an early-life stress model. The pups were pretreated with UA at different administration times (2, 4, and 6 weeks) and doses (50, 100, and 150 mg/kg) from adolescence (PND29). Behavioral tests were performed after the end of the administration. Subsequently, hippocampal samples were collected for histopathological and molecular evaluations. Male offspring rats subjected to maternal separation exhibited increased sensitivity to prepulse inhibition and cognitive impairment, accompanied by severe neuroinflammation and impaired neurogenesis. However, UA attenuated maternal separation-induced prepulse inhibition deficits and cognitive impairments and restored hippocampal neurogenesis in a dose-dependent manner. Furthermore, UA pretreatment preserved dendritic spine density, synapses, and presynaptic vesicles. In addition, it exerted anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting microglial activation and expression of the proinflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-6, and interleukin-1β. Potential mechanisms included upregulation of brain-derived neurotrophic factor protein expression and activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase signaling pathway. This study is the first preclinical evaluation of the effects of UA on cognitive impairment in schizophrenia. The findings suggest that changes in cognitive function linked to schizophrenia are driven by the interaction among neuroinflammation, neurogenesis, and synaptic plasticity and that UA has the potential to reverse these processes. These observations provide evidence for future clinical trials of UA as a dietary supplement for preventing schizophrenia.

studies.title: Urolithin A improves Alzheimer's disease cognition and restores mitophagy and lysosomal functions.
studies.abstract: Compromised autophagy, including impaired mitophagy and lysosomal function, plays pivotal roles in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Urolithin A (UA) is a gut microbial metabolite of ellagic acid that stimulates mitophagy. The effects of UA's long-term treatment of AD and mechanisms of action are unknown. We addressed these questions in three mouse models of AD with behavioral, electrophysiological, biochemical, and bioinformatic approaches. Long-term UA treatment significantly improved learning, memory, and olfactory function in different AD transgenic mice. UA also reduced amyloid beta (Aβ) and tau pathologies and enhanced long-term potentiation. UA induced mitophagy via increasing lysosomal functions. UA improved cellular lysosomal function and normalized lysosomal cathepsins, primarily cathepsin Z, to restore lysosomal function in AD, indicating the critical role of cathepsins in UA-induced therapeutic effects on AD. Our study highlights the importance of lysosomal dysfunction in AD etiology and points to the high translational potential of UA. Long-term urolithin A (UA) treatment improved learning, memory, and olfactory function in Alzheimer's disease (AD) mice. UA restored lysosomal functions in part by regulating cathepsin Z (Ctsz) protein. UA modulates immune responses and AD-specific pathophysiological pathways.

studies.title: Urolithin A reduces amyloid-beta load and improves cognitive deficits uncorrelated with plaque burden in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease.
studies.abstract: In the present study, we investigated the effects of urolithin A (UA), a metabolite generated from ellagic acid via its metabolism by gut bacteria, as an autophagy activator with potential neuroprotective activity. WT and 3xTg-AD mice were administered long-term intermittent dietary supplementation with UA. UA was found to prevent deficits in spatial memory, cued fear response, and exploratory behavior in this model. It also decreased the Aβ plaque burden in areas of the hippocampus where these protein deposits are prominent in the model. Interestingly, correlation analyses demonstrate that Aβ plaque burden positively correlates with enhanced spatial memory in 3xTg-AD mice on a control diet but not in those supplemented with UA. In contrast, Aβ42 abundance in cortical and hippocampal homogenates negatively correlate with spatial memory in UA-fed mice. Our data suggest that plaque formation may be a protective mechanism against neurodegeneration and cognitive decline and that targeting the generation of proteotoxic Aβ species might be a more successful approach in halting disease progression. UA was also found to extend lifespan in normal aging mice. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that UA is able to induce autophagy and to increase Aβ clearance in neuronal cell lines. In summary, our studies reveal UA, likely via its actions as a autophagy inducer, is capable of removing Aβ from neurons and its dietary administration prevents the onset of cognitive deficits associated with pathological Aβ deposition in the 3xTg-AD mouse model as well as extending lifespan in normal aging mice.

studies.title: Urolithin A Attenuates Diabetes-Associated Cognitive Impairment by Ameliorating Intestinal Barrier Dysfunction via N-glycan Biosynthesis Pathway.
studies.abstract: This study aims to investigate the effect of Urolithin A (UA) on diabetes-associated cognitive impairment in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) mouse model induced by high-fat diet (HFD) and streptozotocin (STZ). The UA-treated T2DM mice display an attenuated cognitive impairment as well as reduced levels of metabolic endotoxemia and proinflammatory cytokines in serum. A systemic restraint of gut/brain inflammation in UA-treated T2DM mice is also observed as the downregulation of TLR4 and Myd88 in colon along with the inhibition of GFAP, Iba-1, NLRP3, and inflammation-related genes in brain. Moreover, UA ameliorates gut barrier dysfunction by upregulating tight-junction proteins levels. Furthermore, UA restores the hyperglycemia-mediated downregulation of genes involved in N-glycan biosynthesis both in vivo and in vitro, which plays a crucial role in barrier integrity. Although UA shares similar beneficial effects on diabetes with metformin, unlike metformin, the effect of UA is independent of gut microbiome and short chain fatty acids. Taken together, these data suggest that feeding UA can attenuate diabetes-associated cognitive impairment by ameliorating systemic inflammation and intestinal barrier dysfunction via N-glycan biosynthesis pathway. The study implies UA as a potential novel pharmaceutic target for diabetes therapy via manipulating gut-brain axis and N-glycan metabolism.

studies.title: Urolithin A attenuates memory impairment and neuroinflammation in APP/PS1 mice.
studies.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by an abnormal accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques, neuroinflammation, and impaired neurogenesis. Urolithin A (UA), a gut-microbial metabolite of ellagic acid, has been reported to exert anti-inflammatory effects in the brain. However, it is unknown whether UA exerts its properties of anti-inflammation and neuronal protection in the APPswe/PS1ΔE9 (APP/PS1) mouse model of AD. Morris water maze was used to detect the cognitive function. Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase-mediated dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) assay was performed to detect neuronal apoptosis. Immunohistochemistry analyzed the response of glia, Aβ deposition, and neurogenesis. The expression of inflammatory mediators were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). The modulating effects of UA on cell signaling pathways were assayed by Western blotting. We demonstrated that UA ameliorated cognitive impairment, prevented neuronal apoptosis, and enhanced neurogenesis in APP/PS1 mice. Furthermore, UA attenuated Aβ deposition and peri-plaque microgliosis and astrocytosis in the cortex and hippocampus. We also found that UA affected critical cell signaling pathways, specifically by enhancing cerebral AMPK activation, decreasing the activation of P65NF-κB and P38MAPK, and suppressing Bace1 and APP degradation. Our results indicated that UA imparted cognitive protection by protecting neurons from death and triggering neurogenesis via anti-inflammatory signaling in APP/PS1 mice, suggesting that UA might be a promising therapeutic drug to treat AD.

studies.title: Gut Microbiota-Derived Anandamide Mediates the Therapeutic Effects of Urolithin A on Alcohol-Induced Cognitive and Social Dysfunction via CB1R-DRD2-RAP1 Signali
studies.abstract: Chronic alcohol consumption disrupts the gut microbiome, exacerbating alcohol-induced cognitive and social dysfunction (AICSD), which constitutes a primary etiology of early-onset dementia. Urolithin A (UA) has been well-reported as an effective intervention for neurodegenerative diseases. However, the protective efficacy of UA against AICSD, and its underlying mechanisms remain largely elusive. First, our study demonstrates that UA significantly enhances work memory (60.43%), short-term memory (12-fold), long-term memory (50.32%), social ability (10-fold), and social novelty (12-fold), while concurrently reducing synaptic impairments and neuroinflammation. Moreover, UA restores AICSD by upregulating the dopamine D2 receptor (DRD2) via RAP1 signaling. Furthermore, antibiotic treatment and fecal microbiota transplantation experiments confirm the causality between the host microbiota and behavioral alterations. Treatment with UA-enriched Bacteroids sartorii and Parabacteroids distasonis, or their derived endocannabinoid-anandamide (AEA), also ameliorates AICSD. Finally, AEA inhibits the Rap1 signaling through cannabinoid receptor 1 (CB1R) and DRD2 interaction, eventually ameliorating AICSD. Collectively, our study elucidates that microbiota-derived AEA mediates the therapeutic effects of UA on AICSD through the CB1R-DRD2-RAP1 signaling axis, providing valuable insights for UA and microbiome-targeted endocannabinoid interventions against AICSD.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A small polyphenol metabolite from pomegranate; studied for muscle and mitochondrial health.
explanation.what_it_is: Urolithin A is a small organic compound (molecular formula C₁₃H₈O₄) that your gut bacteria produce when you eat pomegranates, berries, and certain nuts — it's one of the breakdown products of plant chemicals called ellagitannins. It's not naturally abundant in food itself; your microbiome has to convert the precursor molecules into urolithin A. People typically take it as an oral supplement in capsule or powder form, often in doses ranging from 250 to 1000 mg daily in human studies.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Activates mitophagy, a cellular cleaning process that removes damaged mitochondria.
explanation.how_it_works: Urolithin A appears to work mainly by triggering a process called mitophagy — essentially, your cells' way of identifying and recycling damaged mitochondria (the small energy-producing factories inside your cells). When mitochondria age or sustain damage, they become less efficient at producing ATP (the molecule cells burn for energy), and they can leak harmful molecules. By promoting their removal and replacement, urolithin A may help restore the efficiency of energy production in muscle and nerve cells. It also appears to reduce inflammation and oxidative stress (cellular damage from reactive oxygen species, which are harmful byproducts of metabolism). The exact molecular pathways are still being mapped, but the effect on mitochondrial health is the leading mechanism identified in human studies.
explanation.safety_line: Mild, transient tolerability observed in short-term trials; long-term safety data absent.
explanation.safety_detail: The human trials retrieved (lasting 4–12 weeks) reported mild gastrointestinal symptoms and headache in small numbers of participants, with no serious adverse events documented. However, these trials are short, involve modest sample sizes, and have not systematically monitored for harms over months or years. Absence of reported side effects in a short trial is not evidence of long-term safety.
safety_bullets: Long-term safety (beyond 12 weeks) is unknown — no adequately powered extended studies retrieved.
Untested in pregnancy, nursing, and pediatric populations; excluded from all retrieved trials.
Gut microbiota composition affects urolithin A metabolism; people with dysbiosis (imbalanced microbiota) may have different exposure.
Drug interactions (especially with medications metabolized by liver or transported by ABC proteins) have not been systematically studied.
explanation.chem_meaning: Urolithin A is a moderately lipophilic polyphenol (XLogP 2.3), meaning it has some affinity for fatty tissues and cellular membranes but is not purely water-soluble. This moderate lipophilicity allows it to cross cell membranes and reach mitochondrial compartments, which is relevant to its proposed mechanism of action. The molecule's small size and aromatic ring structure make it stable enough to survive digestion and circulation, though it is still subject to metabolism by liver enzymes.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: A 2022 RCT and 2025 RCT (n=42) showed improvements in muscle strength and related biomarkers of mitochondrial function (such as markers of mitochondrial biogenesis) in healthy or recreationally active participants. A 2026 systematic review synthesized these human trials. One 2021 animal study demonstrated that urolithin A induced mitophagy and improved muscle function in a muscular dystrophy model. The human trials lasted 4–12 weeks and used doses ranging from 250–1000 mg daily.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: The grade is Moderate because three human RCTs exist with consistent direction (improvement in strength), but the largest confirmed sample size is ~42 participants in a single trial, making the effect estimate imprecise and vulnerable to small-study bias. A systematic review exists but has not been independently verified or replicated.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four human RCTs (including a 2025 trial with n=42 testing running performance, a 2022 trial on strength and exercise performance, and a 2022 trial examining vascular endothelial function in relation to microbiota) reported improvements in exercise capacity, aerobic performance, and recovery markers. One 2024 animal study in type 2 diabetic mice also showed antidiabetic and metabolic benefits. Studies lasted 4–12 weeks; doses were 250–1000 mg daily in humans.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade reflects consistent improvements across four human trials, but the same precision limitation applies: the largest single-trial sample retrieved is ~42, making the overall effect estimate unstable. No major inconsistency detected, but replication in larger cohorts is needed.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Eleven animal studies (2025–2026) examined urolithin A in models of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, sleep deprivation, cadmium toxicity, and schizophrenia-like behavior. Models showed neuroprotective effects, reduced neuroinflammation, attenuation of autophagy dysfunction, and improvements in cognitive and behavioral readouts. No human trials on cognition were retrieved.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Evidence is entirely animal-derived (rodent and cell models) and does not reliably predict human cognitive outcomes. The mechanisms are plausible (mitophagy, neuroinflammation reduction) but have not been validated in living humans. This is classified Preliminary because human testing is absent.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base for urolithin A is heavily weighted toward human trials for muscle strength and exercise performance (4 RCTs, 2022–2025), though sample sizes are modest (~42 in the largest trial reported). Cognition evidence is entirely animal-derived (11 studies, 2025–2026) and does not yet inform human efficacy. Overall, the compound is supported by short-term human trials (4–12 weeks) in healthy and recreationally active adults, with longer-term and broader population studies absent. The 2026 systematic review on muscle outcomes is the most comprehensive synthesis available, but independent replication is limited.
explanation.open_questions: The records provided do not include trials in older adults (a primary target population for longevity interventions), clinical populations with sarcopenia or neurodegenerative disease, or studies longer than 12 weeks — so durability and real-world clinical benefit remain untested in the records shown. Cognition has no human data whatsoever, making the translation from animal models to symptomatic cognitive outcomes completely open. Gut microbiota composition is recognized as a modifier of urolithin A bioavailability, but no trials stratified by or tested microbiota composition, leaving this a potential source of variable response.

appraisal.headline: Evidence for muscle strength and exercise performance rests almost entirely on a single n=42 trial from 2025, and cognition claims derive wholly from animal studies with no human validation.

concerns.issue: Single-study evidence base for primary claims
concerns.detail: Both muscle strength and exercise performance grades are Moderate, yet only 1 of 4 and 1 of 5 studies respectively report sample sizes, and that single reported n=42 RCT appears in both outcome lists (2025). The 2022 RCT on muscle strength and performance lacks a reported n, and the 2026 systematic review's conclusion is noted as 'not independently replicated or verified.' A single outlier result or methodological flaw in the 2025 trial could substantially shift—or eliminate—the pooled effect estimate.

concerns.issue: No human data for cognition outcome
concerns.detail: All 11 studies graded under cognition are animal-only (10 animal, 1 unclassified); the engine explicitly flags this as 'Indirectness: evidence is animal-only; does not reliably translate to humans.' The median sample size reported is n=15 in animals. No RCT, observational study, or case series in humans exists in this retrieved set. The Preliminary grade reflects this appropriately, but marketing or clinical promotion of cognitive benefits would rest on preclinical evidence alone.

concerns.issue: Median sample size of 42 across all muscular outcomes
concerns.detail: Only 1 of 4 studies reports n for muscle strength and 1 of 5 for exercise performance. The engine notes 'effect estimate may be unstable' at this scale. Small trials are prone to publication bias, outcome switching, and random variation. Without knowing the sample sizes of the remaining 3 muscle-strength and 4 exercise-performance studies, it is impossible to assess whether the Moderate grade reflects a consensus of adequately powered trials or amplification of a single small positive result.

concerns.issue: Recency and lack of replication in human muscle studies
concerns.detail: The human trials span 2021–2026, with the key evidence (2025, n=42 RCT) being the most recent. The 2022 RCT lacks a reported sample size, and the 2026 systematic review is the only attempt at synthesis—but its conclusion 'is not independently replicated or verified,' per the engine. A three-study human evidence base (the unnamed 2022 RCT, the 2025 n=42 trial, and one more) is below the threshold for robust replication.

concerns.issue: Heterogeneous study populations and outcome operationalization not visible
concerns.detail: Study titles suggest variation—'Running Performance' (2025), 'Vascular Endothelial Function' (2022), and unspecified 'muscle strength' in the unnamed 2022 RCT—yet the records do not detail whether these measure the same construct, use comparable instruments, or enrolled comparable populations. Pooled effect is noted as 'none extractable,' which may reflect this heterogeneity or simply lack of quantitative reporting in abstracts. The 2026 unclassified study on cardiac dysfunction may not belong in 'exercise performance' at all.

appraisal.mechanism_check: The proposed mechanism—urolithin A induces mitophagy (selective autophagy of mitochondria), improving mitochondrial function and energy availability—is plausible at the cellular level and supported by animal data (e.g., the 2021 muscular dystrophy study). However, there is a substantial inferential leap from mitochondrial biogenesis in vitro or in rodent muscle to measurable improvements in human exercise performance or strength in healthy adults. The animal cognition studies invoke similar mitophagy and neuroinflammation reduction, but no human trial has measured whether these mechanisms translate to cognitive outcomes; the leap is even larger because cognition depends on neural systems not captured by simple cellular assays.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would argue that the 'Moderate' grades rest on a single n=42 RCT (2025) whose results have not been independently replicated in humans, combined with a 2022 trial of unknown size and a 2026 meta-analysis that itself lacks external verification. The 2022 RCT titles mention mitochondrial biomarkers, not clinical outcomes, suggesting that positive effects may be biochemical signals without functional consequence. Cognition is graded Preliminary and animal-only, appropriately, but the overall 'Moderate' tier may mislead readers into believing human efficacy is established when it rests on a single small, recent, unreplicated trial.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: An adequately powered (n ≥ 100–150 per arm), well-registered RCT in humans measuring muscle strength or exercise capacity as a pre-specified primary outcome, with results replicated in an independent cohort, would ground the Moderate grade. For cognition, a phase IIb RCT in a specific cognitive disorder (e.g., mild cognitive impairment or mild Alzheimer's disease) with a validated cognitive scale as the primary outcome would move the evidence from Preliminary to Exploratory or Moderate.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un pequeño metabolito polifenol de la granada; estudiado para la salud muscular y mitocondrial.
explanation_es.what_it_is: La urolitina A es un pequeño compuesto orgánico (fórmula molecular C₁₃H₈O₄) que las bacterias intestinales producen cuando consumes granadas, bayas y ciertos frutos secos — es uno de los productos de degradación de químicos vegetales llamados elagitaninos. No es naturalmente abundante en los alimentos; tu microbiota debe convertir las moléculas precursoras en urolitina A. Las personas típicamente la toman como suplemento oral en forma de cápsula o polvo, frecuentemente en dosis que varían de 250 a 1000 mg diarios en estudios humanos.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Activa la mitofagia, un proceso de limpieza celular que elimina mitocondrias dañadas.
explanation_es.how_it_works: La urolitina A parece funcionar principalmente desencadenando un proceso llamado mitofagia — esencialmente, la manera en que tus células identifican y reciclan mitocondrias dañadas (las pequeñas fábricas productoras de energía dentro de tus células). Cuando las mitocondrias envejecen o sufren daño, se vuelven menos eficientes en la producción de ATP (la molécula que las células queman para obtener energía), y pueden filtrar moléculas dañinas. Al promover su eliminación y reemplazo, la urolitina A puede ayudar a restaurar la eficiencia de la producción de energía en las células musculares y nerviosas. También parece reducir la inflamación y el estrés oxidativo (daño celular por especies reactivas de oxígeno, que son subproductos dañinos del metabolismo). Las vías moleculares exactas aún se están mapeando, pero el efecto en la salud mitocondrial es el mecanismo principal identificado en estudios humanos.
explanation_es.safety_line: Tolerabilidad leve y transitoria observada en ensayos a corto plazo; datos de seguridad a largo plazo ausentes.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos humanos recuperados (con duración de 4–12 semanas) reportaron síntomas gastrointestinales leves y dolor de cabeza en un pequeño número de participantes, sin eventos adversos graves documentados. Sin embargo, estos ensayos son cortos, involucran tamaños de muestra modestos, y no han monitorizado sistemáticamente los daños durante meses o años. La ausencia de efectos secundarios reportados en un ensayo corto no es evidencia de seguridad a largo plazo.
safety_bullets: La seguridad a largo plazo (más allá de 12 semanas) es desconocida — no se recuperaron estudios extendidos adecuadamente diseñados.
Sin prueba en poblaciones embarazadas, lactantes y pediátricas; excluidas de todos los ensayos recuperados.
La composición de la microbiota intestinal afecta el metabolismo de la urolitina A; las personas con disbiosis (microbiota desequilibrada) pueden tener una exposición diferente.
Las interacciones farmacológicas (especialmente con medicamentos metabolizados por el hígado o transportados por proteínas ABC) no han sido estudiadas sistemáticamente.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: La urolitina A es un polifenol moderadamente lipófilo (XLogP 2.3), lo que significa que tiene cierta afinidad por los tejidos grasos y las membranas celulares pero no es completamente soluble en agua. Esta lipofilia moderada le permite cruzar las membranas celulares y llegar a los compartimentos mitocondriales, lo que es relevante para su mecanismo de acción propuesto. El tamaño pequeño de la molécula y su estructura de anillo aromático la hacen lo suficientemente estable para sobrevivir a la digestión y circulación, aunque aún está sujeta al metabolismo por las enzimas hepáticas.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un RCT de 2022 y un RCT de 2025 (n=42) mostraron mejoras en la fuerza muscular y biomarcadores relacionados de función mitocondrial (como marcadores de biogénesis mitocondrial) en participantes sanos o activos recreacionalmente. Una revisión sistemática de 2026 sintetizó estos ensayos humanos. Un estudio animal de 2021 demostró que la urolitina A indujo mitofagia y mejoró la función muscular en un modelo de distrofia muscular. Los ensayos humanos duraron 4–12 semanas y utilizaron dosis que variaban de 250–1000 mg diarios.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación es Moderada porque existen tres RCTs humanos con dirección consistente (mejora en la fuerza), pero el mayor tamaño de muestra confirmado es ~42 participantes en un solo ensayo, haciendo que la estimación del efecto sea imprecisa y vulnerable al sesgo de estudios pequeños. Existe una revisión sistemática pero no ha sido verificada independientemente ni replicada.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro RCTs humanos (incluyendo un ensayo de 2025 con n=42 probando rendimiento en carrera, un ensayo de 2022 sobre fuerza y rendimiento del ejercicio, y un ensayo de 2022 examinando la función endotelial vascular en relación con la microbiota) reportaron mejoras en la capacidad de ejercicio, rendimiento aeróbico y marcadores de recuperación. Un estudio animal de 2024 en ratones diabéticos tipo 2 también mostró beneficios antidiabéticos y metabólicos. Los estudios duraron 4–12 semanas; las dosis fueron 250–1000 mg diarios en humanos.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación Moderada refleja mejoras consistentes en cuatro ensayos humanos, pero aplica la misma limitación de precisión: el tamaño de muestra más grande de un solo ensayo recuperado es ~42, haciendo que la estimación del efecto general sea inestable. Ninguna inconsistencia importante detectada, pero se necesita replicación en cohortes más grandes.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Once estudios animales (2025–2026) examinaron la urolitina A en modelos de enfermedad de Alzheimer, enfermedad de Parkinson, deprivación del sueño, toxicidad por cadmio y comportamiento tipo esquizofrenia. Los modelos mostraron efectos neuroprotectores, reducción de neuroinflammación, atenuación de disfunción de la autofagia, y mejoras en resultados cognitivos y del comportamiento. No se recuperaron ensayos humanos sobre cognición.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia es enteramente derivada de animales (modelos en roedores y células) y no predice confiablemente los resultados cognitivos humanos. Los mecanismos son plausibles (mitofagia, reducción de neuroinflammación) pero no han sido validados en humanos vivos. Se clasifica como Preliminar porque falta la prueba en humanos.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia para la urolitina A está fuertemente ponderada hacia ensayos humanos para fuerza muscular y rendimiento del ejercicio (4 RCTs, 2022–2025), aunque los tamaños de muestra son modestos (~42 en el ensayo más grande reportado). La evidencia de cognición es enteramente derivada de animales (11 estudios, 2025–2026) y aún no informa la eficacia humana. En general, el compuesto está apoyado por ensayos humanos a corto plazo (4–12 semanas) en adultos sanos y activos recreacionalmente, con estudios a largo plazo y en poblaciones más amplias ausentes. La revisión sistemática de 2026 sobre resultados musculares es la síntesis más completa disponible, pero la replicación independiente es limitada.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados no incluyen ensayos en adultos mayores (una población primaria para intervenciones de longevidad), poblaciones clínicas con sarcopenia o enfermedad neurodegenerativa, o estudios más largos que 12 semanas — así que la durabilidad y el beneficio clínico en el mundo real permanecen sin probar en los registros mostrados. La cognición no tiene datos humanos en absoluto, haciendo que la traducción de modelos animales a resultados cognitivos sintomáticos esté completamente abierta. Se reconoce que la composición de la microbiota intestinal es un modificador de la biodisponibilidad de la urolitina A, pero ningún ensayo estratificó o probó la composición de la microbiota, dejando esto como una fuente potencial de respuesta variable.

appraisal_es.headline: La evidencia para la fuerza muscular y el rendimiento del ejercicio descansa casi enteramente en un único ensayo n=42 de 2025, y las afirmaciones sobre cognición derivan completamente de estudios en animales sin validación humana.

concerns.issue: Base de evidencia de un único estudio para reclamaciones primarias
concerns.detail: Tanto los grados de fuerza muscular como rendimiento del ejercicio son Moderados, sin embargo solo 1 de 4 y 1 de 5 estudios respectivamente reportan tamaños de muestra, y ese único ensayo n=42 reportado parece en ambas listas de resultados (2025). El ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2022 sobre fuerza muscular y rendimiento carece de un n reportado, y la conclusión de la revisión sistemática de 2026 se anota como 'no replicada o verificada independientemente.' Un único resultado atípico o defecto metodológico en el ensayo de 2025 podría cambiar sustancialmente—o eliminar—la estimación del efecto agrupado.

concerns.issue: Sin datos humanos para el resultado de cognición
concerns.detail: Los 11 estudios calificados bajo cognición son solo en animales (10 en animales, 1 no clasificado); el motor explícitamente señala esto como 'Indirectness: la evidencia es solo en animales; no se traduce de manera confiable a humanos.' El tamaño de muestra mediano reportado es n=15 en animales. No existe ensayo clínico aleatorizado, estudio observacional, o serie de casos en humanos en este conjunto recuperado. El grado Preliminar refleja esto apropiadamente, pero la promoción comercial o clínica de beneficios cognitivos descansaría únicamente en evidencia preclínica.

concerns.issue: Tamaño de muestra mediano de 42 en todos los resultados musculares
concerns.detail: Solo 1 de 4 estudios reporta n para fuerza muscular y 1 de 5 para rendimiento del ejercicio. El motor anota 'la estimación del efecto puede ser inestable' a esta escala. Los ensayos pequeños son propensos a sesgo de publicación, cambio de resultados, y variación aleatoria. Sin conocer los tamaños de muestra de los 3 estudios restantes de fuerza muscular y 4 de rendimiento del ejercicio, es imposible evaluar si el grado Moderado refleja un consenso de ensayos adecuadamente potenciados o amplificación de un único resultado positivo pequeño.

concerns.issue: Recencia y falta de replicación en estudios musculares humanos
concerns.detail: Los ensayos humanos abarcan 2021–2026, con la evidencia clave (ensayo clínico aleatorizado 2025, n=42) siendo la más reciente. El ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2022 carece de un tamaño de muestra reportado, y la revisión sistemática de 2026 es el único intento de síntesis—pero su conclusión 'no es replicada o verificada independientemente,' según el motor. Una base de evidencia humana de tres estudios (el ensayo clínico aleatorizado no nombrado de 2022, el ensayo n=42 de 2025, y uno más) está por debajo del umbral para replicación robusta.

concerns.issue: Poblaciones de estudio heterogéneas y operacionalización de resultados no visible
concerns.detail: Los títulos de estudios sugieren variación—'Running Performance' (2025), 'Vascular Endothelial Function' (2022), y 'fuerza muscular' no especificada en el ensayo clínico aleatorizado no nombrado de 2022—sin embargo, los registros no detallan si estas miden el mismo constructo, utilizan instrumentos comparables, o reclutaron poblaciones comparables. El efecto agrupado se anota como 'ninguno extraíble,' lo cual puede reflejar esta heterogeneidad o simplemente falta de reportaje cuantitativo en resúmenes. El estudio no clasificado de 2026 sobre disfunción cardíaca podría no pertenecer a 'rendimiento del ejercicio' en absoluto.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: El mecanismo propuesto—la urolitina A induce mitofagia (autofagia selectiva de mitocondrias), mejorando la función mitocondrial y disponibilidad de energía—es plausible a nivel celular y respaldado por datos en animales (ej., el estudio de distrofia muscular de 2021). Sin embargo, existe un salto inferencial sustancial desde biogénesis mitocondrial in vitro o en músculo de roedores hacia mejoras medibles en el rendimiento del ejercicio humano o fuerza en adultos saludables. Los estudios de cognición en animales invocan mitofagia similar y reducción de neuroinflammation, pero ningún ensayo humano ha medido si estos mecanismos se traducen en resultados cognitivos; el salto es aún más grande porque la cognición depende de sistemas neurales no capturados por ensayos celulares simples.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico argumentaría que los grados 'Moderados' descansan en un único ensayo clínico aleatorizado n=42 (2025) cuyos resultados no han sido replicados independientemente en humanos, combinado con un ensayo de 2022 de tamaño desconocido y un metanálisis de 2026 que carece en sí mismo de verificación externa. Los títulos del ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2022 mencionan biomarcadores mitocondriales, no resultados clínicos, sugiriendo que los efectos positivos podrían ser señales bioquímicas sin consecuencia funcional. La cognición se califica como Preliminar y solo en animales, apropiadamente, pero el nivel 'Moderado' general puede llevar a los lectores a creer que la eficacia humana está establecida cuando descansa en un único ensayo pequeño, reciente, no replicado.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado adecuadamente potenciado (n ≥ 100–150 por brazo) en humanos, bien registrado, midiendo fuerza muscular o capacidad del ejercicio como resultado primario preespecificado, con resultados replicados en una cohorte independiente, fundamentaría el grado Moderado. Para cognición, un ensayo de fase IIb en un trastorno cognitivo específico (ej., deterioro cognitivo leve o enfermedad de Alzheimer leve) con una escala cognitiva validada como resultado primario movería la evidencia de Preliminar a Exploratoria o Moderada.
